You do not have the power to free yourself from it. You may struggle, as some of you say you are doing, but it still overcomes you. He knows all about that. Yet He approves of the struggle, the effort, the watchfulness, and the determination. When He saves you, He will give you the power, and then you will stand instead of falling, because He Himself will uphold you. Now you know that you have come this far. You know that if you had the power right now to completely destroy the hold of that evil habit over your life forever, you would do it without a moment's hesitation. You say, “Oh yes, I would. If only I had the power.” That is repentance. That is genuine repentance. What you cannot do for yourself, Christ meets you where you are and says, “I will do it for you. I will break the power of that habit. I will deliver you from the hand of the enemy. I will free you from that bondage. Only place your faith in Me, and I will lift you up. I will fill you with My Spirit. You shall stand in Me and by Me, and what you are now struggling to do for yourself, I will do for you.” Then you have come this far—that you hate sin? “Yes, I do.” You have written it in your letters to me, and others are saying it who have not written. “Yes,” you say, “I desire to be saved from it. If I could save myself from sin this very moment and never sin again, I would do so.” Would you? Is that not repentance? What else could it be? Suppose you had a disobedient and rebellious son. He had lived in defiance of your authority, wasted your money, and trampled your commands underfoot. Then suppose he comes to see the error of his ways. Perhaps suffering opened his eyes. Perhaps poverty did. Perhaps it was something else. In any case, he sees it. He comes home and says: “Father, what a fool I have been. How wicked I have been. I see it all now. I did not see it when I was doing it. I see my sinful course, the sins that caused you grief and brought sorrow to your life. Oh, how I hate it all. I repent in dust and ashes. Father, I forsake it all. I come home to you.” What would you say? Would you say, “My son, you have not repented enough. Go away and come back when you feel more sorrow”? No. Your father's heart would reach out in love and forgiveness. You would embrace him and welcome him home. “Just so, I tell you, there is joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents” (Luke 15:10, ESV). There would be joy in that family over the return of the wandering child. But suppose the son said: “Father, I truly repent and forsake my sins, but there are companions who may influence me again, and there are habits so powerful that I fear they may overcome me. Let me stay close to you. I need your strength.” What would you say? Would you not answer: “Then come in, my son. Stay with me, and I will protect you. I will help you. You shall not walk alone. I will be with you and uphold you.” As far as any human father could protect another, you would protect your son. He would never lack your sympathy or support, day or night. Your heavenly Father lacks neither sympathy nor strength. His eye never sleeps. His arm never grows weary. You need only bring your helpless weakness to His almighty strength through this act of faith, and He will uphold you, even if a legion of devils surrounds you. Lastly, you renounce your sins—that is, in your will, purpose, and determination. You say, “I never want to grieve Him again.” You sing it, and you mean it. “I do not want to grieve Him anymore.” If you could live without grieving Him, you would count every sacrifice worthwhile. Is that not repentance? You know it is. You renounce sin. You do not say, “Lord Jesus, save me while I hold on to this right hand and this right eye. Save me while I cling to these forbidden things.” No. You say, “Lord Jesus, save me from them. Make me clean.” That is repentance. You see sin. You hate sin. You renounce sin. Now then, believe in the Lord Jesus Christ. Oh, Holy Spirit, reveal the simple way of faith. You ask, “How am I to believe?” A troubled soul once asked me this question in large letters: “How am I to believe?” How does a bride believe in her husband when she gives herself to him at the marriage altar? She entrusts herself to him. She believes in him. She enters into a covenant with him and then goes home and lives as though that covenant is true. That is faith. How do you trust a physician when you are sick and lying on your bed, whether in peace or suffering? You place your case in his hands. You commit yourself to his care. You trust his skill and follow his instructions. Have faith like this in Jesus Christ. Trust and obey, and expect that it will be with you according to His Word. Instead, the faith of many people is like that of a person suffering from a serious illness. They believe He can heal the disease of sin on His appointed terms. They believe that He shows no partiality. They believe that He has saved hundreds who were just as sinful as they are. Yet for some reason they do not trust Him. They hold back. What you need to do is place your case in His hands and say: “Lord Jesus, I come as You have invited me, confessing and forsaking my sin. If I could, I would leave it behind forever this very moment. You know that I come renouncing it, yet without the power to save myself from it. And now, Lord Jesus, You have said, ‘Whoever comes to me I will never cast out’” (John 6:37, ESV). “I do come. You do not cast me out. You receive me. Blessed Heavenly Father, I give myself to You. I place my sins upon the sacrifice of Your Son. You have said that You will receive me and forgive me for His sake. Now I roll my guilty burden onto Him, and I believe Your promise. I trust You to be true to Your Word.” That is faith. “But,” said a dear lady, “I do not feel it.” No. You must trust first. Notice carefully: you are not first to believe that you are saved, but to believe that He is saving you now according to His promise. “Whatsoever you ask in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours” (Mark 11:24, ESV). That is the principle of faith. Believe that you receive before you feel. When you receive, then you will feel. God will prove true, and every person or devil who contradicts Him will be found a liar. Throw your arms around the Crucified One. Take hold of the hand of the Son of God. Bring your guilty soul to the foot of His cross and say: “You receive me. You forgive me. You cleanse me. You save me.” Keep speaking the language of faith. I have seen many souls enter into freedom while repeating these precious words personally: “He was wounded for my transgressions; he was crushed for my iniquities; upon him was the chastisement that brought me peace, and with his stripes I am healed” (Isaiah 53:5, ESV). Keep speaking the language of faith all the way home tonight. Go into your room and say: “I am determined to be saved, if salvation is truly offered to me.” Resolve that if you perish, you will perish there at the foot of the cross, pleading for mercy. But you will not perish, for He has promised mercy to those who come. I have never known a soul to come to this point and not soon find salvation. Get into the lifeboat. Leave behind the wreck of your own righteousness and your own efforts. Step fully into the lifeboat of Christ's sacrifice. Father!” (Romans 8:15, ESV), and you know with certainty that you have passed from death to life (John 5:24, ESV). May the Lord help you. Amen.

fields.title: Love
fields.body_html:
“So now faith, hope, and love abide, these three; but the greatest of these is love.” — 1 Corinthians 13:13 It must be a precious thing to be greater than faith and greater than hope—it must indeed be precious! And just in proportion as things are valuable and precious among people, so much effort and risk will people take to counterfeit them.

I suppose that in no area of dishonesty in this dishonest world has more time and ingenuity been spent than in making counterfeit money, especially banknotes. Just as wicked people have tried to imitate the most valuable products of human skill for their own profit, so the devil has been trying from the beginning to counterfeit God's most precious things and produce something so similar that people generally would not see the difference. Perhaps in no area has he been more successful than in producing a counterfeit love. I almost think he has perfected it in these days. I do not think he could improve much on the present imitation.

This love—this love—is God's most precious treasure. It is dearer to His heart than all the vast realms of His universe—dearer than all the glorious beings He has created. So much so that when some of the highest spirits among the angelic hosts violated this love, He cast them from the highest heaven to the lowest hell.

Why?

Not because He did not value those wonderful beings, but because He valued this love more. He saw that it was more important for the well-being of His universe to preserve the harmony of love in heaven than to spare those spirits who had allowed selfishness to disrupt it.

So our Lord says: “I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven.” (Luke 10:18, ESV) The day is coming when He will also see all the terrible results of that first rebellion fall. Hasten that glorious day!

But let us consider for a few moments this precious and beautiful love. Let us first try to define it.

What is it?

First: It Is Divine It must be shed abroad in the heart by the Holy Spirit.

We look in vain for this heavenly plant among unrenewed people. It does not grow in the corrupt soil of human nature. It springs up only where the plow of true repentance has broken up the hard ground of the heart, where faith in a crucified Savior has purified it, and where the blessed Holy Spirit has taken permanent possession.

It is the love of God—not merely love for God, but a love that is like God, comes from God, and is directed toward the same purposes and objects that He loves.

It is a divine work planted in the heart by the Holy Spirit.

Perhaps some of you are saying, “Then it is useless for me to try to cultivate it, because I do not have it.”

Exactly.

You may cut, prune, and water forever, but you can never cultivate what has not been planted.

Your first need is to have this love poured into your heart.

One of the great errors of this age is the belief that human nature only needs pruning, improving, and developing, and then it will turn out right.

No, no!

“Every plant that my heavenly Father has not planted will be rooted up.” (Matthew 15:13, ESV) If you want this divine love, you must break up the fallow ground of your heart and invite the heavenly Husbandman to come and sow it there—to pour it into your soul.

Second: It Is a Divine Principle I want you to notice that this love is a divine principle, distinct from mere natural affection.

All people have love as a natural instinct. They naturally love those they like or those who treat them well.

“For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same?” (Matthew 5:46, ESV) Wicked people love one another through natural affection, just as a tiger loves its cubs.

There is great confusion among religious people on this subject. They feel pity and generosity toward their fellow human beings, and they may even give their possessions to feed the poor, yet not possess a spark of divine love in their hearts.

Saul, after God departed from him, was not entirely without generous feelings toward his family and kingdom.

The rich man in hell had some concern for his brothers.

But neither of them possessed a spark of this divine love.

Be careful that you are not deceived. Millions are.

Let us notice one or two points where counterfeit love and divine love completely and permanently differ in nature.

First: Counterfeit love is Selfish Counterfeit love is selfish. It is never exercised except to satisfy some selfish motive in human nature. Thousands of motives may inspire it—far too many to list—but we will consider two or three.

We read in this chapter that a person may give away all his possessions to feed the poor and even surrender his body to suffering, yet still be without true love.

What a surprising thought.

Yet there are many examples showing that such a thing is possible.

First, a person may do these things to support and promote a favorite system of belief to which he has become devoted. Just as people become absorbed in politics or in what they consider the good of their nation, they may even be willing to face great danger in order to advance their cause.

Further, a person may do such things in an effort to earn eternal life. Paul did this when he sought to establish his own righteousness. Later he tells us that self was the driving force behind all his zeal. It was all for his own advancement. There was no divine love in it. At that time he was unrenewed, without Christ, and selfish, even while he was doing those things.

Or, third, a person may act simply to satisfy a naturally generous disposition.

I used to say to a generous friend of mine, when he spoke confidentially about his giving and the pleasure it brought him, attributing it entirely to divine grace, “Wait, my friend. I am not sure it is all grace. You enjoy giving more than some people enjoy receiving. Be careful that you do not lose your reward by failing to examine where your gifts are going. Do not give your money to every cause that comes along. Remember that you are accountable to God for your resources, and that God will require an account of how you have used them.”

True love takes the time to examine different needs and seeks the best opportunities to give for God's glory and for the salvation of people.

Do not automatically attribute your generosity to the Holy Spirit if it is not of that kind, for you will receive no reward for it, either in this life or the next.

False love begins with self and ends on earth.

Here is one way to distinguish it from God's love.

The devil's love focuses primarily on the earthly side of human beings and gives less importance to the spiritual side. In this respect it directly opposes divine love, which views people as whole beings and always gives first importance to the soul.

We see plenty of counterfeit charities these days.

The other day I picked up a so-called religious publication and read the glowing praise it gave to a certain man who had recently died. I thought to myself, would anyone imagine this was a Christian publication in a Christian country?

There was not the slightest recognition of a soul. There was no reference to the man's spiritual condition or eternal destiny. One or two ordinary human qualities were highlighted and praised until he appeared to be something extraordinary. But there was no mention of a soul, no mention of God who will judge him, and no mention of heaven or hell.

People often say, when speaking about godless or even wicked individuals, “You must be charitable. You must not judge.”

Satan does not care how much of this one-sided love exists. The more there is, the better it serves his purpose. It makes people more comfortable in their sins and helps lead them more easily toward destruction.

My friends, are you more concerned about relieving temporal distress than you are about feeding famished souls? If you are, you may know where your love comes from! Don't misrepresent me, and say that I teach all of one, and none of the other. God forbid, for, if any man "has this world's good, and sees his brother in need, and shutters up his bowels of compassion from him, where is the love of God in him?" But, on the other side, if he sees him spiritually famishing—dying for want of the bread of life—where is the love of Christ in him, if he does not minister to this spiritual destitution? I know that real Christianity cares for body and soul. Bless God, it does; but, always mind that it sets the soul FIRST. I know the Master fed the multitude; but, before that, He had them with Him three days, trying to save their souls, and when they got hungry in the process, then He made them sit down, and fed their bodies. He always looked after the soul first, and so does everyone possessed of Divine love.

Why? Because Divine love has opened his eyes. He realises the value of souls. He sees them famishing. He sees them being damned, and he cannot help himself. His desire to save them rushes out of him like a torrent; he beholds them, and has compassion on them. Try your love by this mark: Do you contemplate the dying, famishing, half-damned souls of your fellow-men? Do you look abroad on the state of the world, and the state of the church? Do you think about it? Do you go into your closet, and spread it before the Lord, as Hezekiah and Jeremiah and Hosea did? Do you look at it, and turn it over, and weep over it, and pray and cry, as Daniel and Paul did? Try yourselves, my brethren, my sisters, by this mark.

Divine love is always centered on that great question of infinite love: Matthew 16:26 : “For what will it profit a man if he gains the whole world and forfeits his soul?

Or what shall a man give in return for his soul?”

Oh, I can never get it out of my ears or away from my heart! How clearly I see the emptiness and vanity of everything compared with the salvation of the soul! What does it matter if a man dies in a poorhouse—if he dies on a doorstep, covered with sores like Lazarus—what does it matter if his soul is saved? It is your belief as much as mine that the soul is immortal, and that the death of the body is only its entrance, if it is saved, into a glorious future of everlasting joy, progress, and holiness.

Does a child remember how he used to cry over his lessons when he becomes a man? Does he dwell on all the little difficulties of his school days when he is enjoying the benefits they brought him? In the same way, all our sufferings, trials, and sorrows here will seem far less important if we save our souls and help save the souls of others.

This divine love makes everything else serve the salvation of souls; it uses everything else to save and bless the inner and spiritual person. Do you remember the occasion when the Master had fed the multitudes, and when they came to Him again to be fed, He said: “Truly, truly, I say to you, you are seeking me, not because you saw signs, but because you ate your fill of the loaves.” John 6:26 You might have said, “Quite right; the people want food; they are hungry.” But do you hear the divine sorrow expressed in these words—that they were so spiritually dull that they valued earthly bread more than heavenly bread? Give people as much physical bread as you can, but make sure you give them spiritual bread first, for this is a mark of true love.

Do you have this love? Every soul knows whether it does or not. People are often so unreasonable in matters of religion; they talk about not knowing. But you can discover in two minutes whether you love God or yourself more. Tell me that a woman does not know whether she loves her husband or herself more! Nonsense! What is the proof? She seeks to please him and is willing to sacrifice herself for him; in fact, she makes his interests her own.

Do you love God most? Are you willing to set aside your own interests and seek His? Do you have this divine love, born from Heaven and leading to Heaven? If not, my friend, determine that you will have it now. Begin to cry earnestly to God for the Holy Spirit to pour it into your heart. Give up your arguments and excuses, and come to the foot of the cross and ask Him, “Come, Lord, break up this poor, sinful heart of mine, and pour this beautiful, pure, divine love into it.” Then you will no longer seek your own interests, but the things that belong to Jesus Christ.

fields.title: Love And Rebuke
fields.body_html:
“So now faith, hope, and love abide, these three; but the greatest of these is love.” 1 Corinthians 13:13 The second main difference between true and false love that we want to point out is this: Divine love is not only consistent with reproof and rebuke, but it often requires them from those who possess it. It makes it the duty of those who have it to reprove and rebuke whatever is evil— whatever does not promote the highest good of the person concerned.

In this, as in everything else, this love follows its divine example: “Those whom I love, I reprove and discipline, so be zealous and repent.” Revelation 3:19 When necessary for a person's good, God reproves and disciplines. He does not willingly afflict or grieve people any more than a father willingly disciplines a disobedient child. But if he is a wise father, he will do so because he loves the child. In the same way, the person who possesses this Divine love is willing to rebuke and reprove sin wherever it is found. He will not allow sin to remain unchallenged in his neighbor, but will faithfully reprove him and seek to lead him to what is right.

Let us look at a beautiful example (one among many) of this Divine love at work in the heart and life of the very apostle who wrote 1 Corinthians 13. We cannot go wrong in choosing this example because it comes from Paul himself.

“But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face, because he stood condemned. For before certain men came from James, he was eating with the Gentiles; but when they came he drew back and separated himself, fearing the circumcision party. And the rest of the Jews acted hypocritically along with him, so that even Barnabas was led astray by their hypocrisy. But when I saw that their conduct was not in step with the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas before them all, ‘If you, though a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you force the Gentiles to live like Jews?’” Galatians 2:11–15 Well done, Paul—what noble and courageous love! He did not go and whisper behind Peter's back or attack him in secret.

"I said to Cephas before them all..."

If you want a characteristic of true love, here it is.

It must have been extremely painful for Paul to rebuke Peter publicly. They loved one another. In fact, years later Peter referred to Paul as: “...our beloved brother Paul...” 2 Peter 3:15 They truly cared for one another. Paul understood the demands of true love, for he wrote this thirteenth chapter of Corinthians. If he loved Peter, and if he understood true love, why did he openly rebuke him? Why did he put himself through the pain of doing so?

Faithfulness to Peter, faithfulness to the truth, and faithfulness to Jesus Christ required it.

Therefore, Paul set aside his own personal feelings and endured the pain of confrontation rather than allow Peter to continue in error, the Gentile believers to be misled, and the Jews to be influenced by worldly compromise.

Paul publicly rebuked Peter because truth was at stake. As often happens, truth was with the minority. Most of the influence was on the side of the circumcision party. They were among the most influential believers, yet Paul stood against that influence in his rebuke of Peter.

Why?

Because faithfulness to the truth demanded it, and Divine love is first pure .

There is an even greater example in our Lord Himself—the Master whose entire soul was love and whose life was a continual sacrifice for the good of others. Yet how faithfully He corrected His own followers when they strayed from the truth, and how fearlessly He exposed and condemned the shallowness and hypocrisy of those who claimed to love God while contradicting that claim by their lives.

How fearlessly He rebuked sin wherever He found it.

On one occasion He said to His disciples: “But he turned and rebuked them.” Luke 9:55–56 (The longer wording found in some older translations— "You do not know what manner of spirit you are of. For the Son of Man came not to destroy men's lives but to save them" —is not included in the ESV text.)

It was as though He was saying, "You should understand this by now."

On another occasion He said: “Are you also still without understanding?” Matthew 15:16 And again: “Get behind me, Satan! You are a hindrance to me. For you are not setting your mind on the things of God, but on the things of man.” Matthew 16:23 That was Divine love. That was faithful love—love that was willing to rebuke rather than allow its object to continue in sin and offend God.

Again, when speaking to the Pharisees and others who claimed to be faithful to God, He said: John 8:39, 42, 44 “If you were Abraham's children, you would be doing the works Abraham did.”

“If God were your Father, you would love me, for I came from God and I am here.”

“You are of your father the devil, and your will is to do your father's desires.”

It was no easier for Jesus Christ to confront the religious people of His day than it is for His servants to confront professing believers who live inconsistently today.

Yet His divine heart was overflowing with love. He gave Himself on the cross for them and prayed: “Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.” Luke 23:34 Oh, that your love and mine would not lack this feature of the divine likeness! If only there were more of this faithful, loving love that dares to reprove sin and lovingly rebuke a brother, instead of the false love that flatters a person to his face and criticises him behind his back.

Do you suppose that most professing Christians of this generation truly believe that one another are living rightly? Consider almost any church. Do you think that most members genuinely believe that their fellow members—brothers and sisters in the faith—are living consistently godly lives, not merely outwardly but in heart?

Sadly, what people say behind one another's backs often tells a different story. They do not really believe it. They know better, and they are quick to tell others about the faults they see. Yet not one in a thousand has ever gone privately to a brother, taken him by the hand in love, and gently reproved him concerning his sinful or backsliding conduct.

What would people think of a woman who, after attending church the previous day, requested a private meeting with Mrs. —— and, when alone with her, said with tears in her eyes and deep sincerity: “Dear Mrs. ——, I have come to see you on a very difficult matter. Will you allow a word of encouragement and correction from someone who feels very weak and unworthy, yet trusts that the Spirit of God has led her to come? May I tell you that I was troubled by your conduct at church yesterday. It seemed to me that your attention was not focused on the seriousness of the service, but was occupied with observing and criticising the dress of the person sitting opposite you. I also noticed that when you left the church, you immediately began laughing and talking in a way that seemed inconsistent with the service you had just attended.”

Suppose she continued: “Dear Mrs. ——, I have not mentioned this to anyone—not even to my husband—but I have come to speak to you personally. Let us go before the Lord together and ask Him to give us His Holy Spirit, so that He may show you where you are wrong and reveal whether you are drifting away from the love of God.”

What would people think? What would they say about such conduct?

Yet if everyone who saw sin in a neighbor would act in this way—if they would follow the Lord's instruction and go privately to their brother or sister and point out the fault—how many people would be saved from backsliding, and how many painful divisions and controversies in churches could be avoided!

But where are the people who will do it?

I do not mean that there are none—God forbid. I know there are some. But comparatively speaking, where are they? Where is the person willing to endure personal discomfort in order to help another?

That is the real issue. If it were an easy and pleasant duty, many would perform it readily. But because it is painful, they hesitate to do it.

Where is the person who will do it rather than allow a brother to remain asleep in sin? Where is the person who will act rather than see the cause of Christ dishonored and harmed? Where are the saints who, in humility and love, go to restore someone who has gone astray?

I hope you know many such people. Sadly, I know only a few. If you know many, I am glad, and the more you know, the better. If you are one of them, then that is one more. If every Christian possessed this kind of love, what a transformation would soon take place. This is what the church needs—people who can afford to rebuke and correct because they are not concerned with what others think of them. Their only concern is to please their Lord and Master and do His will.

Do you have this love that seeks not its own interests?

What a contrast there is between Saul and Paul. Have you ever considered it? What does Saul say?

“For, being ignorant of the righteousness of God, and seeking to establish their own, they did not submit to God's righteousness.” Romans 10:3 Before he received true love, his driving motive was self-interest. He was not concerned with the kingdom of God; he was concerned with his own honor, reputation, and advancement. He wanted the approval of his nation.

Now compare that with Paul after his conversion. What does he say?

“That I have great sorrow and unceasing anguish in my heart. For I could wish that I myself were accursed and cut off from Christ for the sake of my brothers, my kinsmen according to the flesh.”

Romans 9:2–3 There is love indeed.

These were the very people whose approval he once desired. Yet after receiving the Holy Spirit and having his eyes opened to see their lost condition, he grieved deeply for them. He says: “That I have great sorrow and unceasing anguish in my heart. For I could wish that I myself were accursed and cut off from Christ for the sake of my brothers, my kinsmen according to the flesh.”

Romans 9:2–3 What a contrast!

He no longer cares what they think of him. Instead, he goes about trying to open their eyes, showing them that religious privilege alone cannot save them and that they must turn to God. Self has completely disappeared from view. Paul's heart, soul, and efforts are now devoted to the salvation of others.

If people praise him, he accepts it. If they condemn him, he accepts that too. His focus is the kingdom of God, and regardless of how people treat him, he continues seeking that kingdom— even to the point of martyrdom. He endures their fiercest hatred and opposition so that he might help turn people from Satan to God and from sin to righteousness.

Self is no longer the center. It is no longer Paul who matters—it is Christ and His kingdom.

False love is the opposite.

The person who possesses false love is mainly concerned about what people think of him, not about how they treat his professed Lord. Such a person cannot bear the thought of correcting anyone. The very idea frightens him. He calls those who do so harsh, legalistic, or judgmental. Yet he may have no hesitation in criticising someone behind their back.

The speech of false love reveals its true nature. It flatters with its lips. Honey is on its tongue, but poison lies underneath. Beware of it.

Even when it appears to praise a brother or neighbor, it often adds a destructive qualification: “Oh, he is a good man, but...”

“Yes, I respect him greatly, only...”

How much damage has been done by such words! How many good reputations have been tarnished by this spirit! How much influence for good has been weakened or destroyed by careless criticism and hidden malice!

It has been truly said that there is scarcely any virtue so pure that slander will not try to stain it.

Even in the lives of godly people, those looking for faults can always find something to criticise.

Therefore, be careful which love you possess.

True love does not rejoice in wrongdoing.

“It does not rejoice at wrongdoing, but rejoices with the truth.” 1 Corinthians 13:6 Are you aware of a feeling of satisfaction when someone you dislike falls into sin or misfortune?

If so, be careful. That spirit is not from God.

Do you secretly rejoice when evil comes upon an enemy? If so, you must get rid of that poison.

God will not allow such a spirit in Heaven. One person carrying that bitterness would corrupt Paradise itself. Our Lord said: “But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be sons of your Father who is in heaven.” Matthew 5:44–45 Now, my brother, my sister, examine yourself.

We shall meet again, and you will discover that these are not imaginary ideas or empty theories.

They are realities. Though these great truths of Christianity are not often preached in our day, they remain true. They are found in the Word of God, and there is no true Christianity in us unless we possess this love that hates evil because it is evil, that lovingly reproves it, seeks to remove it, and longs to see it healed.

Here again, false love is the complete opposite of Divine love. It does not care much about righteousness. Its highest ideal is simply peace and quiet. It says, “Let us keep things calm; we must not disturb the peace of the church.” It cries, “Peace, peace,” when there is no real peace.

It says, “We cannot help these problems. Everyone must look after himself. We are not responsible for our neighbor.”

Often it knows very well that serious wrongs exist beneath the surface—wrong practices, harmful systems, and sinful conduct that it chooses to tolerate or support. But because these things are hidden from public view, it says, “Leave them alone. We must not stir things up. Peace! Peace!”

It says, “Never mind righteousness; the church must be supported, regardless of where the money comes from. Never mind the wrongs that may be connected with it. We must have peace.”

It would rather cover up evil than expose and remove it. It says, “Never mind. We cannot allow these matters to be investigated, corrected, or rooted out. Peace—we must have peace!”

Then, if someone dares to expose the problem and reveal the corruption underneath, they are treated as Elijah was treated by Ahab.

“When Ahab saw Elijah, Ahab said to him, ‘Is it you, you troubler of Israel?’” 1 Kings 18:17 In the same way, those who confront wrongdoing are often accused of causing division rather than those responsible for the wrongdoing itself.

And when you remind people of the great principle: “So whatever you wish that others would do to you, do also to them, for this is the Law and the Prophets.” Matthew 7:12 They sometimes reply, “But we are not expected to be perfect in this life,” and use that as an excuse to avoid dealing with the issue. In this way, they simply place another covering over the problem and allow it to continue.

This is the devil's love, and the more of it there is, the better it serves his purpose.

But the love and wisdom that come from above are different.

“But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, open to reason, full of mercy and good fruits, impartial and sincere.” James 3:17 Notice that it is first pure, then peaceable .

I would rather live in continual conflict alongside what is true, right, and good than enjoy harmony with what is empty, corrupt, and evil, and destined for destruction.

May the Lord help you to make the same choice.

fields.title: Love And Conflict
fields.body_html:
“So now faith, hope, and love abide, these three; but the greatest of these is love.” 1 Corinthians 13:13 Another characteristic of this Divine love is that it often involves conflict .

It was so with our Lord. He was the very embodiment of it. He was love itself, and grace and truth flowed continually from His lips. His blessed feet went about doing good, and His hands ministered to the needs and happiness of people. Yet His entire journey through this fallen world was marked by conflict, opposition, and persecution. His mission was to bring peace on earth, but the result was a sword! Why?

Not because He desired it. He would no doubt have preferred to live at peace with all people, as His apostle urges us to do, “so far as it depends on you.” More than that, He was the Prince of Peace! Then why was there opposition, conflict, and even deadly hostility wherever He went?

Because people resisted and rejected His divine and heavenly ministry. They would not receive His correction or His teaching because it exposed and condemned their ways. They would not listen to His voice because they were of their father the devil, and they desired to do their father's works. Therefore, they persecuted Him and sought to kill Him.

This was the reason—not that He wanted it to be so, but it was the result of people's resistance to the beautiful, heavenly, and divine truths He taught. And it is the same today with that truth and with those who embody it.

Jesus Christ living again in His people , as they demonstrate His principles before the world, obey His teachings, and live for the same purposes for which He lived, will produce the same result everywhere. It must be so while humanity remains divided into two groups—the righteous and the wicked, those born of the flesh and those born of the Spirit. One side must yield, or there will be ongoing conflict and struggle.

It was so with the Savior, and perhaps it is so with some of us.

I believe this is often a stumbling block to God's sincere people. Many of them do not like the feeling that their hand seems to be against everyone and everyone's hand against them, or nearly so. They do not like the feeling of isolation. They do not enjoy being compelled to take a course that many professing Christians around them condemn and describe as uncharitable.

As a result, they often examine themselves to see whether they may somehow be mistaken in following the Divine Spirit. They say with Jeremiah, and with the Jeremiahs of every age: “Woe is me, my mother, that you bore me, a man of strife and contention to the whole land!”

Jeremiah 15:10 They feel like "speckled birds, against whom all the birds around are gathered." They feel this opposition and conflict deeply. But what are they to do?

Very often, when following the leading of the Divine Spirit, it is impossible to avoid such consequences. We have to march through opposing forces. We have to become the object of widespread suspicion.

But what then?

Must we give up?

Must we refuse to walk in the blood-stained footsteps of the Captain of our salvation?

Must we reject the honor of serving in the front ranks of the Lamb's army because of conflict, pain, or persecution?

No, never.

Let those who are being led by the Divine Spirit into paths that involve conflict continue faithfully.

Follow on, brother! Follow on, sister!

There is perhaps no area in which those who desire to live wholeheartedly for God suffer more than this. They continually say, "My friends object." Often these friends are Christians.

People come to see me, or write to me, saying that the Spirit of God has been urging them toward a certain course of action for months or even years, yet they are held back by the opinions and wishes of parents, brothers, sisters, uncles, aunts, or Christian friends.

I believe it will be found on the great Day of Judgment that more blessed endeavors have been crushed, more leadings of the Holy Spirit disobeyed, and more promptings of the Spirit suppressed through the influence of so-called Christian friends than through all other influences combined.

“Lord, let me first go and bury my father.” Luke 9:59 (ESV, adapted from the account) This remains a common excuse for those whom the Lord calls into more demanding paths of Christian service.

Oh, my friends, I am convinced of it.

Be careful, fathers and mothers, brothers and sisters, and relatives of every kind.

Do not misunderstand me.

Carefully weigh, test, and examine your impressions and desires before God. Go into your prayer closet and lay them before the Lord. Search your own heart. Make sure there is no self-interest, no pride, no desire for recognition, or longing to do something unusual merely for its own sake.

Take all the time necessary to become fully persuaded that it is God's call.

But once you are convinced, then even if fathers, mothers, brothers, sisters, husbands, wives, or friends object, move forward, my brother, and God will vindicate you.

If, twenty years ago, I had waited for Christian friends to approve and open the door for me, I would still be waiting today. The souls that God, in His infinite mercy, has entrusted to me would never have been gathered.

I did not wait for human approval of my Master's call. Instead, I said: "Lord, if I die trying, I will do it."

And He rarely allows people to perish while pursuing His will. He stands with them and grants abundant fruit from their labor.

A lady said to me recently, "You know my father is a Christian, and I am afraid of going against him."

"Yes," I replied, "that is a proper feeling, and I respect it."

But she was a mature woman, and so I asked, "Is your father as concerned about the interests of God's kingdom as he ought to be?"

She replied, "I dare not say that he is."

"I suppose," I said, "he is growing older and has perhaps lost some of the vigor and enterprise of his younger days, when he wanted to go out and win everyone he could for Christ."

"Yes," she replied, "his zeal for the kingdom of Jesus Christ has greatly declined."

Then I said, "God holds you responsible just as He holds any other person responsible. He does not have one standard for men and another for women. There will not be separate judgment seats because of human traditions. God will hold you accountable for obeying the teaching of His Spirit and the leading of His providence just as much as He would your brother."

"What answer will you give if you refuse? You may find yourself in the position of the man who said, 'Lord, let me first go and bury my father.'"

She replied, "I am afraid I shall."

Now, let us settle this matter, you Protestant Christians who are here.

Because Roman Catholicism has abused the principle that a person may have to leave father, mother, house, or land for Christ's sake, does that mean we Protestants should abandon the principle altogether?

Has it come to this—that a person is only expected to follow Christ when everyone approves, says "Amen," and when doing so appears to secure his own interests?

If that were true, I would give up religion altogether and simply live for my own pleasure.

I once said to a lady, "When you gave yourself to the Lord Jesus Christ, you entered into a relationship with Him similar to that of a wife to her husband."

What woman would believe she should obey her father and mother instead of her husband? It would be considered unreasonable. How much less should she obey her father when his wishes directly oppose God's clear leading?

We are to obey our parents in the Lord , but thousands of fathers and mothers are preventing their children from fully serving God.

Oh, what will you say to God when your precious children stand before Him without the harvest they might have gathered and the souls they might have won?

What will you say then?

Why do you hold them back?

Often, the reasons are things people would be embarrassed to admit publicly.

Is it fear of suffering?

In many cases, it is not. But even if it is, did you make an agreement with Jesus Christ when you dedicated yourself and your children to Him that they would never suffer for His sake?

Is it pride?

Is it because you desire for them the approval and praise of this world?

Be careful. God often disciplines His people in the very areas where they place worldly interests above His kingdom.

But you say, "Everyone will be against me."

Perhaps they will.

Let us settle that from the beginning.

Count all such things as loss. Do not allow them to move you.

You say, "It will be a life of conflict until the end."

Perhaps it will. It was so for Him.

You say, "I am so weak."

He knows that completely.

You say, "It hurts so much when people criticise me and speak against me."

Yes, it hurts. But if that is the path He calls you to walk, He will also give you the grace to endure it.

“Blessed are you when others revile you and persecute you and utter all kinds of evil against you falsely on my account.” Matthew 5:11 “Yet if anyone suffers as a Christian, let him not be ashamed, but let him glorify God in that name.” 1 Peter 4:16 The Lord does not usually show us the entire path ahead. Therefore, we can only move forward one step at a time.

The future may appear uncertain, but once we are fully persuaded that the next step is the one God wants us to take, we should take it and leave the future in His hands.

Come out as Abraham did, not knowing where you are going, and as surely as God reigns on His throne, He will vindicate your obedience. The very things you think you have sacrificed for Him may become part of the reward He gives for your faithfulness.

I have seen many examples of this.

I have known daughters who were turned out of their fathers' homes because they followed the leading of the Spirit of God. They endured persecution, trials, and suffering. Yet when those fathers reached the end of their lives, they often wanted no one else to pray with them except those same daughters.

The way to win the hearts of parents is through a consistent, steadfast, and holy devotion to the Lord Jesus Christ.

If you compromise, adjust your convictions to please others, or hesitate when God calls, you may miss the reward.

Do people recognise inconsistency?

Yes, they do.

They quickly say, "That is not genuine religion."

But if you are consistent and wholehearted, God can use that very faithfulness to win the souls of those about whom you are deeply concerned.

Furthermore, a false love shrinks from opposition.

It cannot endure persecution.

One sure mark of false love is that it is always found on what appears to be the winning side—not necessarily the side that will ultimately triumph, but the side that seems popular and successful at the moment.

When truth is honored, respected, and crowned with praise, this false love loudly declares its loyalty.

But when truth is despised, when its followers are few, weak, and poor, then it quietly withdraws its support.

I sometimes think that many who speak loudly about the glory of God and the honor of religion would have struggled had they been placed in the judgment hall with Jesus among the mocking soldiers.

I wonder what their zeal for God's glory would have looked like when it threatened their own reputation.

Many people are enthusiastic when their glory and Christ's glory seem to advance together.

But when the crowd cries, “Away with him, away with him, crucify him!” John 19:15 Then they become more concerned with protecting themselves than standing with Him.

True love remains loyal to the Lord Jesus in humiliation as well as in triumph.

It stands with Him when He is staggering beneath the cross, just as readily as when the crowds are spreading branches and shouting, “Hosanna!” Matthew 21:9 I fear that many people use the name of Christ merely as a means of advancing their own interests.

May God keep us from being among them.

This false love never willingly goes to prison for truth.

You never find it at the stake.

Before the cost becomes too great, it usually changes sides or alters its position.

It is never found in disgrace.

It is never found standing with Christ when He is in the minority.

It is absent at Golgotha.

It avoids the cross.

Yet it eagerly joins the celebration when Christ appears triumphant.

I often wonder how many of us would remain faithful if times of persecution returned.

How many would endure imprisonment?

How many would stand for the truth while being mocked, ridiculed, and hated by the crowd?

How many would have remained with Him on the road to the cross?

How many would have stood beneath the cross while people mocked Him, spat upon Him, divided His garments among themselves, and shook their heads, saying: “He saved others; he cannot save himself.” Matthew 27:42 How many of us would have remained faithful then?

Yet, as surely as we live, that is the kind of love that will endure the test of the Day of Judgment.

Oh, have you received this love? Love in the darkness. Love in the garden. Love in sorrow. Love in suffering. Love in isolation. Love in persecution. Love even unto death. Do we have this love?

Examine yourselves, beloved, and see whether you are truly in the faith. There is great need for such examinations these days, when there are so many false gospels and so much false teaching.

We hear much about being "complete in Him" from people who may never have truly known Him at all, and who understand its meaning no more than a small kitten lying by the fireplace.

I say again, examine yourselves. Are you truly in the faith? Are you truly in Christ?

For it is no easier now to be a genuine follower of Christ than it ever was.

Furthermore, false love refuses to call things by their proper names.

Consider the many ways in which wrongdoing is excused among professing Christians. Think of the comfortable and self-indulgent attitudes people adopt toward ungodly trades and practices.

What do I mean?

I mean businesses that cannot be used to serve the interests of Christ's kingdom—businesses that prosper by appealing to sinful desires or by encouraging ungodliness.

How politely false love renames such things. How easily it gives respectable titles to practices that harm the bodies, hearts, and souls of people.

And when Divine love speaks against these things, false love responds: "But we must consider our own interests. We have much at stake."

Indeed, you do have much at stake.

And when the Judge rises to defend those who have been harmed and oppressed by such unjust practices, you may discover that what you gained on earth has become a burden too great to bear.

May the Lord have mercy on anyone who makes a living from the sins, weaknesses, or destruction of others.

Leave such practices as quickly as possible.

Separate yourselves from them.

Do not allow yourself to be comforted by the false love that tries to make you feel at ease while participating in wrongdoing. Such a spirit has nothing in common with Divine love. Rather, let us say with Scripture: “O my soul, come not into their council; O my glory, be not joined to their company.” Genesis 49:6 Let us keep ourselves separate from every alliance between light and darkness, truth and falsehood.

“Take no part in the unfruitful works of darkness, but instead expose them.” Ephesians 5:11 And remember: “For behold, the day is coming, burning like an oven, when all the arrogant and all evildoers will be stubble. The day that is coming shall set them ablaze, says the Lord of hosts.”

Malachi 4:1 God is still the same God.

He does not change.

Let us call things by their right names.

Let us face evil honestly.

Let us drive it out of the world—or at least out of the church.

The Lord will test and expose everything.

I can almost hear the warnings of divine judgment approaching. I can see signs of God's displeasure gathering against nations and churches that refuse to repent.

If a nation continues in sin, and if the church refuses to separate itself from practices that dishonor God, it should not presume upon His favor.

Has God treated other nations lightly when they rejected His ways?

Do we imagine that we are less accountable than those who came before us?

Were not the people of Jerusalem judged despite the privileges they had received?

And have we not received even greater light and opportunity?

Are there not similarities between many religious people today and the Pharisees of old?

Did not Jesus condemn those who appeared religious outwardly while exploiting the weak?

Even today, are there not people who speak piously while acting unjustly toward others?

Could not God's words still apply where such conditions exist?

“Ah, sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, offspring of evildoers, children who deal corruptly!” Isaiah 1:4 And is it not still true in some places that: “The prophets prophesy falsely... and my people love to have it so.” Jeremiah 5:31 Perhaps someone says, "Surely we are not that bad."

Then look around.

Observe carefully.

Has it not sometimes become a common saying that some people would rather do business with anyone than with a professing Christian?

And sadly, has there not sometimes been reason for such criticism?

Should we be surprised when unbelievers mock the church if Christians do not consistently demonstrate honesty and integrity?

Can we say that every business transaction is conducted fairly?

Do people always charge what is just and reasonable?

Or do many take advantage of others whenever the opportunity arises and then call it acceptable?

Whether the amount involved is small or large, taking unfair advantage of another person is still wrong.

God places extortion among serious sins.

May the Lord help me to live according to His Word: “Let each of you look not only to his own interests, but also to the interests of others.” Philippians 2:4 May I have the love that refuses to take unfair advantage of my neighbor simply because I have the opportunity.

May I never dishonor the precious name of Jesus Christ while claiming to be one of His followers.

It is time for this false and self-serving love to be removed.

The first and most essential principle of true love is righteousness.

There is no true love apart from righteousness.

If your love is incompatible with righteousness, it is not from God.

If God has shown you something in your life that is wrong, then say: "Lord, let Your light shine fully upon it. I am grateful that You have revealed it while there is still time to change. Bring Your knife to it. Cut it away, even if its roots run deep into my heart. I want it removed completely."

Will you do that?

Will you allow God to make you truthful, upright, and clean?

Will you allow Him to make you more like Himself?

Will you be filled with His pure and holy love toward God and toward all people?

This is what the Lord desires for you.

This is why He sent His Son.

Not to provide a superficial way into heaven while leaving us unchanged, but to transform us into the people He intends us to be.

And He is able to do it.

The Great Physician is willing.

He has enough love.

Enough power.

Enough grace.

Trust your whole heart to Him.

Will you allow this Divine love to be formed within you?

It will make you willing to suffer.

Willing to endure hardship.

Willing to bear shame, contempt, and persecution.

It will make you willing to do all that human strength can do and endure all that human strength can endure so that the purposes for which Christ came may be accomplished and the progress of His glorious kingdom may advance.

fields.title: Love And Loneliness
fields.body_html:
“So now faith, hope, and love abide, these three; but the greatest of these is love.” 1 Corinthians 13:13 The possession of this Divine love often requires walking a lonely path.

Not only does it bring opposition and persecution, but sometimes it means facing those things alone. Once again, Jesus, the perfect example of Divine Love, stands before us as our model.

He was often alone.

Even the disciples He had drawn closest to Himself, and to whom He had tried to impart His thoughts and spirit, frequently failed to understand Him. He often had to correct them and grieve over their lack of understanding and sympathy.

In the greatness of His love, He went forward alone into the darkness of Gethsemane while His disciples slept. Then He continued through mockery, scorn, and suffering all the way to the cross.

Sadly, He was almost entirely alone, except for a few faithful women who remained with Him— to their everlasting honor.

As it was with the Master, so it has been with all those whom God has called to move ahead of their generation.

It was true of John, Paul, many of the apostles, and countless others whom God has called into extraordinary paths of service.

When John received the Revelation concerning things yet to come, he had to go alone to the island of Patmos.

When Paul was caught up into the third heaven and heard things too sacred to be spoken at that time, he went alone and could not even share all that he had experienced.

Those whom God calls to advance often have to walk ahead of others.

And so it is today.

When God calls His followers into a new or unusual path, they often find themselves walking where few have gone before.

Greater love often requires a lonelier walk.

You may say, "That seems very hard."

Yes, I know it does.

I wish I could make it easier, but I cannot change the fact.

Greater love often requires some measure of loneliness because it is those who draw closest to the Lord who receive His deeper confidences.

If you desire intimate fellowship and confidential communion with your Master, you must remain close to His heart. You cannot experience that from a distance.

And when God gives someone greater light than those around them, and that person chooses to follow that light, it naturally places them ahead of others.

Unless they can persuade and encourage others to follow—which is often difficult—they must continue on alone.

A beautiful example of this is found in Acts 10.

Peter was called to move ahead of the entire church.

God had a new step for His kingdom, and He chose Peter to take it.

First, God lowered the sheet filled with animals and commanded Peter to consider what he saw.

Peter carefully studied the vision until God had fully gained his attention.

Then came the command: “Rise, Peter; kill and eat.” Acts 10:13 God was teaching Peter that His plans for the kingdom were larger than Peter had imagined.

Peter learned that his responsibility was not to argue with God's directions but to obey them.

Once Peter understood the lesson, he followed God's leading.

But as often happens, many in the church were shocked.

The very church that had once benefited from new acts of God was now suspicious of something new itself.

They questioned Peter and called him to account for his actions.

Peter simply explained what God had done.

And thankfully, they possessed enough wisdom, love, and love to accept his explanation and glorify God.

Would to God we saw more of that spirit today.

Only recently, a lady wrote to me about her husband. She said he sympathised with outreach efforts but insisted that everything people need can already be found within the existing church structure.

Others say much the same thing.

As a result, they oppose anyone who dares to step outside the familiar routine and try something new for the sake of reaching people.

You may explain to them that traditional methods are not reaching everyone.

You may point out the vast numbers of people outside the church who remain untouched by the Gospel—the Gentiles of our generation.

You may show them that these people still need salvation and the cleansing power of the Holy Spirit.

You may demonstrate that your methods are just as biblical and lawful as theirs, and perhaps even more effective.

You may tell them that the Holy Spirit has placed a burden upon your heart and that you feel compelled to act.

Yet instead of rejoicing and glorifying God, they criticise and oppose you.

False love cares more about the method than the result.

It is often more concerned with public opinion than with the advancement of Christ's kingdom.

This is one way to recognise it.

Are you more concerned about what your neighbor thinks, what a minister thinks, or what some respected religious leader thinks than you are about seeing Christ's kingdom advance?

If so, be careful.

That is not the right kind of love.

True love focuses on the goal—the spread of righteousness, the salvation of souls, and the reign of Christ.

It is not overly concerned with methods, provided those methods are lawful and pleasing to God.

I do not suggest doing wrong in order to accomplish good—God forbid.

But Divine love says: "Anywhere with Jesus."

In a church building or outside one.

By the sea or in the marketplace.

On a mountain or in a city street.

Anywhere, Lord Jesus, if only You will take Your inheritance and reign in the hearts of people.

True love is willing to become all things to all people if by doing so it may win some.

It gladly stoops to help those of low position.

It puts its arms around the needy and seeks to bring them to the cross and back into fellowship with God.

It is not concerned with the criticism of religious spectators.

Its focus is on saving the lost.

Like the Good Samaritan, it pours in oil and wine, lifts up the wounded, and seeks their restoration.

It is determined to help, regardless of what others may think.

Have you received this kind of love?

It is wonderful.

It warms the heart.

Its beauty becomes more evident every day.

And it will be even more precious when life comes to an end.

Faith and hope will one day give way to sight and fulfillment, but love will remain forever.

Yet this kind of love requires someone to lead the way.

Are you willing to go first?

Are you willing to endure the hardships of a pioneer?

Can you bear ridicule and criticism from others?

Will you follow where the Holy Spirit leads and trust God with the consequences?

If so, blessed are you.

You will gather a harvest of precious souls.

You will shine forever in God's presence.

But if you continually draw back, you place yourself in danger.

Step out onto the ocean of Divine Love.

It alone can carry your fragile vessel through life's storms.

It can make you more than a conqueror.

So step forward.

Follow.

Follow.

Follow.

Do not be afraid.

False love is very different.

It craves human recognition.

Attention and praise are its lifeblood.

Stop noticing it, and it soon fades away.

Paul described this spirit when speaking of his former life: “Being ignorant of the righteousness of God, and seeking to establish their own, they did not submit to God's righteousness.” Romans 10:3 Before his conversion, Saul saw the growing movement of Christ's followers as an opportunity to gain approval and recognition.

Since Christians were widely opposed, Saul believed that persecuting them would increase his own standing.

So he became fiercely hostile toward them, pursuing them even into distant cities.

But later he recognised that the driving force behind his actions had been self-glory.

False love hates being in the minority.

It prefers the safety of popular opinion.

Its followers cling tightly to tradition and are greatly influenced by what respected leaders think.

Like the Pharisees, they continually ask: “Have any of the authorities or the Pharisees believed in him?” John 7:48 My friends, let this teach us wisdom and love.

Test everything carefully before condemning it.

Saul sincerely believed he was serving God when he persecuted Christians.

Yet he was terribly mistaken.

While imagining that he was doing God's work, he was actually opposing God's purposes.

If he had recognised the truth, he would have changed immediately.

I wish more people would remember that many of the practices they now consider respectable and established were once viewed as dangerous innovations.

The paths our spiritual forefathers fought to establish were once considered new, controversial, and unacceptable.

If our forefathers had refused every new leading of God simply because it was unfamiliar, many of the blessings we enjoy today would never have come.

Instead of merely admiring the faith and courage of previous generations, we should imitate them.

They did not spend their lives preserving comfort.

They advanced God's kingdom.

They moved forward in faith.

They pressed on toward the conquest of the world for Christ.

Yet today, many build monuments to past heroes while resisting the very spirit that made those heroes great.

It is much as it was in Jesus' day: “So you witness against yourselves that you are sons of those who murdered the prophets.”

Matthew 23:31 Sadly, much of the same spirit still exists today.

The labels may have changed, but the attitudes often remain the same.

Now, my friends, examine yourselves.

Which love do you possess?

Do you rejoice whenever Christ's kingdom advances through lawful means?

Or are you more concerned about appearances than transformed lives?

Would you rather see a sinner remain in bondage than be rescued through methods that seem unconventional?

Would you rather people be lost respectably than saved unexpectedly?

If so, then the spirit of the Pharisees is still present.

For your instruction, carefully read Matthew 23:23–28 and allow God to search your heart.

Another way this false love reveals itself is in how harshly it often responds in personal situations.

Let us consider an example.

Suppose there is a family of respectable, church-going people who have attended church or chapel for many years. Or imagine a church of the same kind. Nothing unusual has happened. They fear the Lord, live comfortably, and continue much as they have for ten or fifteen years, simply replacing those who have moved away or passed on.

Now suppose that someone in that family or church experiences a genuine spiritual awakening.

Perhaps they read a book, attend a special meeting, or hear a message that God uses to shine fresh light into their heart. They become deeply aware of their spiritual condition. They begin praying earnestly, seeking God, and grieving over their failures. Then they experience afresh the forgiveness of their sins and the joy of God's salvation.

Almost immediately, once this inward work takes place, an outward opportunity opens before them.

The Spirit of God impresses upon them some new area of service—perhaps something long neglected or never previously recognised in their family or church. They see how greatly it could contribute to the salvation of souls and the advancement of Christ's kingdom, and the desire to pursue it begins to burn within them.

They pray over it carefully and wait until they are fully convinced that it is not merely a passing emotion but a genuine leading of the Spirit of God.

Filled with love, faith, and zeal, they go to their minister or a Christian friend. They expect encouragement and support.

But sadly, they are often met with objections.

People begin raising concerns: "Well, that is not quite how we do things."

"That would be outside our usual practice."

"I am afraid the church leaders may object."

"Something might go wrong."

And if the person happens to be young—as though youth itself were a fault—they are often discouraged even further.

They are told: "Wait until you have more experience."

Or: "You should not attempt anything unless we fully approve of it."

My friends, you smile because you know how often this happens.

How many promptings of the Holy Spirit have been silenced this way?

How many heavenly callings, as clear to the heart as Peter's vision was to him, have been dismissed?

How many God-given dreams for advancing Christ's kingdom have been crushed by this false, selfish, and counterfeit love?

May God remove it from among us.

Personally, I would not care what the Lord called my child to do if it would advance His kingdom and glorify His name.

I might say: "My child, this may be difficult for me. I might have chosen a different path for you. But if you are convinced that God is leading you, then go forward, and I will do all I can to help you."

Why?

Because I want the King to receive what belongs to Him.

I want Christ's purposes accomplished, and I desire that He use not only me but also those most precious to me for His glory.

Fathers and mothers, take heed.

If you withhold your children from God, you place yourselves in a dangerous position.

“Those who honor me I will honor, and those who despise me shall be lightly esteemed.” 1 Samuel 2:30 Be careful not to withhold from God what is most precious.

Be careful not to receive His grace in vain.

Sadly, some do.

The fifth area in which Divine love and false love differ is this: Divine love is law-abiding.

By this I mean that it always operates in harmony with God's moral law.

It never does wrong in order to accomplish good.

You will never hear true love say: "I know this is not exactly right, but I can accomplish a good result by doing it."

Never.

That reasoning does not come from God.

Righteousness is woven into the very heart of Divine love.

Just as justice and righteousness are the foundation of God's throne, righteousness lies at the center of true love.

Divine love will never sacrifice righteousness for peace, popularity, convenience, or any other advantage.

What, then, is humanity's duty?

“He has told you, O man, what is good; and what does the Lord require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?” Micah 6:8 When the Holy Spirit produces these qualities in a person's life, God looks upon them with approval, and they walk in the light of His favor.

Do justice.

Love mercy.

Walk humbly with God.

Much of our duty is contained in those words.

Do you hear this, you who constantly compromise God's standards?

You who say that Christians must become more like the world in order to win the world?

You who argue that we must lower ourselves to the world's standards in order to bring people to God?

I tell you plainly: all unrighteousness is sin, and what of those who use false love to excuse sins that are destroying countless lives?

What of those who create laws and systems that protect injustice while claiming to act for the common good?

Let us ask a simple question: Is it just to sacrifice one group of people—especially the weaker and more vulnerable—for the supposed benefit of another group?

Is that justice? Is that mercy? And notice that I say supposed benefit. For history repeatedly shows that injustice never produces lasting good. Can one part of society be oppressed without consequences eventually returning upon the oppressor?

Has that ever happened?

Will it ever happen?

Not while God rules His universe.

No amount of clever reasoning can cancel God's moral law.

“Do not be deceived: God is not mocked, for whatever one sows, that will he also reap.”

Galatians 6:7 No one escapes that principle.

The final characteristic of true love that I will mention is this: It perseveres despite ingratitude, opposition, and persecution.

The person who possesses this love seeks the good of others not merely because it is a duty, but because their heart has been transformed.

Their heart is aligned with God, truth, and righteousness.

Because they love what is right, they cannot stop seeking to help others love it as well—even when those people reject, misunderstand, or despise them.

Jesus demonstrated this love perfectly.

Even while suffering on the cross, He prayed: “Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.” Luke 23:34 His heart remained committed to bringing humanity back to God.

He never turned back.

His love carried Him all the way to death.

Paul followed his Master's example.

Although some people loved him less the more he loved them, he continued seeking their highest good.

He loved them—not their praise, approval, or admiration.

False love behaves differently.

It quickly grows weary when its efforts are not appreciated.

Its attitude becomes: "I have done enough. The kinder I am, the worse people treat me. I will stop helping until I receive more appreciation."

Why?

Because self-glory is the life of false love.

When gratitude and admiration disappear, false love soon dies.

So which kind of love do you possess, my brother?

My sister?

I once heard of a young and successful businessman who attended a service where he heard straightforward biblical truth.

When someone later asked him what he thought, he shifted uncomfortably and replied: "Well, it was dreadful. If what I heard is true, then I am on my way to hell."

Yet perhaps that realisation was the very beginning of hope for him.

Now let me ask you: Do you possess this Divine love?

Remember, as I said at the beginning, it does not naturally grow in the unrenewed human heart.

If you have not experienced the transforming work of the Holy Spirit, then you must begin there.

No matter how many outward imitations you possess, they cannot replace the love of God.

Do you have it, brother?

Do you have it, sister?

If not, you can receive it today.

Will you seek it?

We were all once without it.

“We all once lived... and were by nature children of wrath, like the rest of mankind.”

Ephesians 2:3 We loved and hated according to selfish interests.

But God renews hearts.

He makes us, in some measure, like Christ Himself.

Of Him it is written: “You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness beyond your companions.” Hebrews 1:9 The more you love righteousness and hate evil, the greater your joy will be, and the stronger your testimony for God.

You will be able to say with David: “I have not hidden your deliverance within my heart; I have spoken of your faithfulness and your salvation; I have not concealed your steadfast love and your faithfulness from the great congregation.” Psalm 40:10 When people truly receive this love, they naturally want to share it.

It overflows.

It cannot remain hidden.

As our Lord said: “The water that I will give him will become in him a spring of water welling up to eternal life.” John 4:14 And as Scripture declares: “Many waters cannot quench love.” Song of Solomon 8:7 Have you received this love?

Has it lifted you above your selfish interests?

Or do you still evaluate every opportunity by asking first how it will affect you rather than how it will affect the kingdom of God?

And to you who know that you do not yet possess it: There is hope.

Christ's heart is full of compassion toward you.

He is waiting to pour this love into your soul.

The feast is prepared.

Everything is ready.

Come into His banqueting house.

Rest beneath His banner of love.

And abide there forever.
